content.title: About
content.content: Iced coffee, brewed, decaffeinated is a refreshing beverage made from specially processed coffee beans that have had the caffeine removed. The preparation involves cold‑water extraction (cold brew) for 12–24 hours, after which the concentrate is chilled and served over ice.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cold brew delivers a smoother, less bitter flavor profile compared with hot‑brewed coffee.
Decaffeination is usually performed by water‑process or CO₂ extraction, preserving most aromatic compounds.
Cold‑brew retains more antioxidants than hot coffee due to the long, low‑temperature steeping.
U.S. sales of decaf cold brew have grown over 30% in the past five years.
The drink is often served with milk, cream, or flavored syrups, but its pure taste shines best without additives.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: The lack of caffeine makes the beverage suitable for caffeine‑sensitive individuals and allows enjoyment of coffee flavor without sleep disruption.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cold brew preserves high levels of chlorogenic acids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Served cold and often unsweetened, it contributes to daily fluid intake.

items.title: May support heart health
items.content: Moderate coffee consumption, including decaf, has been linked to a reduced risk of cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Gentle on stomach
items.content: The absence of caffeine and lower acidity make it less irritating for sensitive stomachs.

items.title: Possible additives
items.content: Commercial products may contain sugar, flavorings, or preservatives that increase calories and could trigger allergies.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Although less acidic than hot coffee, the drink can still affect a very sensitive stomach if consumed in excess.

items.title: Storage safety
items.content: An opened bottle of cold brew can lose aroma quickly and become a breeding ground for bacteria if left at room temperature.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the decaf cold brew over ice, add milk, plant‑based cream, or flavored syrup to taste. It also works as a base for cocktails, smoothies, or dessert sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the finished beverage refrigerated in a sealed container for up to 5–7 days. Flavor and aroma deteriorate over time; discard if it becomes sour or shows mold.
